top.title: Houston Rockets beat Golden State Warriors in wild one that included Marcus Smart throwing a punch
top.description: Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) shot in the first half of game action at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Even with Stephen Curry playing just six minutes before leaving with an injury, the Houston Rockets and Golden State Warriors played their usual chaotic battle. The Rockets survived against the short-handed Warriors with a 115-108 victory Wednesday at Toyota Center, but not before they lost Marcus Smart for throwing a punch at Charles Bassey. When the dust settled the Rockets (9-3) dealt the Warriors (8-4), who were on an eight-game winning streak, their first loss since Oct. 24. Amen Thompson had a huge third quarter for the Rockets, scoring 15 of his 19 points in the third. Kevin Durant led Houston with 20 points. Alperen Şengün finished an assist shy of a triple-double with 19 points, 13 rebounds and 9 assists. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg finished with 25 points and 10 rebounds. Things got tense late in the third quarter, when Smart went face-to-face with the Warriors' big man during a dead ball. After the two exchanged words, Smart unleashed a right hand that appeared to graze Bassey's cheek. Smart was ejected, but already had walked off the court and into the tunnel, knowing his fate. Bassey made one of two free throws after the fracas to cut the Rockets' lead to 85-77. The Warriors showed further life early in the fourth quarter with Georges Niang and De'Anthony Melton hitting back-to-back 3-pointers to get within three points with nine minutes remaining. However, the Rockets scored eight straight, including two 3s by Reed Sheppard to stretch the lead back to double digits. When Curry, who entered the night averaging 30.6 points per game, went out with abdominal soreness just six minutes into the game, it looked like it might be a stress-free night for the Rockets. Curry went to the locker room midway through the first quarter with the Warriors trailing 19-10. With no Curry to chase all over the court, Houston stretched that lead to 35-20 by the end of the first quarter. However, Curry being out seemed to unlock Lendeborg, the early front-runner for Rookie of the Year. The 11th pick in the draft out of Michigan scored 18 points in the first half, all coming after Curry's injury. He scored in a variety of ways, knocking down a couple 3-pointers, while also working the boards and getting out on the break. Lendeborg keyed a 9-2 run late in the first half that tied the game, hitting a 26-footer and a midrange jumper during the run that knotted things at 49. The Rockets closed the half with a 7-2 run of their own to enter halftime with a 56-51 edge. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. top.title: Houston Astros' Yordan Alvarez wins AL's Hank Aaron Award among accolades at MLB Awards
top.description: Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez, pictured with MLB Network's Siera Santos at Wednesday's awards show, took home the prestigious Hank Aaron Award as well as three other accolades on the eve of the MVP announcement. (Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) LAS VEGAS - Yordan Alvarez was named the American League recipient of this year's Hank Aaron Award on Wednesday night in another nod to the Houston Astros slugger's prolific season. The Hank Aaron Award recognizes the top offensive performer in each league. Alvarez joins Jose Altuve as Astros players to win the award, which was introduced in 1999 to mark the 25th anniversary of Aaron breaking Babe Ruth's career home-run record. Altuve won the award in 2017 , the same year he was named the American League Most Valuable Player. Alvarez will learn Thursday whether he joins Altuve and Jeff Bagwell as Astros players to win a league MVP award. Alvarez garnered multiple honors at the MLB Awards show, which was held Wednesday night in Las Vegas with the slugger attending in person. Alvarez was also named AL Comeback Player of the Year, the Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter and the All-MLB First Team designated hitter. Winners of the Hank Aaron Award were announced with Billye Aaron - the widow of Hank Aaron, who died in 2021 - among those on stage. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs was voted the National League winner. Alvarez delivered a brief comment on stage after he was named the AL winner. "It means a lot for me, especially because I wear the number 44," Alvarez said, referencing the number also worn by Aaron, at the awards event streamed by MLB.com. "I've been working really hard for this moment and it's really special for me to be part of and see my name on this trophy." To determine the Hank Aaron Award winners, a panel of 10 former winners and Hall of Famers vote on the list of 10 finalists from each league. Astros Hall of Famer Craig Biggio was part of this year's panel. Fans were allowed to vote from the list of finalists, as well. After playing in just 48 games in 2025 due to hand and ankle injuries, Alvarez this season led the majors in batting average (.316), on-base percentage (.432) and slugging percentage (.601), becoming the third Astros player to win a league batting title. Alvarez tied for second in the AL in home runs (42) and ranked second in runs batted in (106), recording career-high marks in both. He led the majors with 109 walks, including 33 intentional walks, and played in a career-high 158 games. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. top.description: Three of Licking County’s best volleyball players certainly measured up to the best in Ohio. Newark Catholic’s Leah Caudill and Sophia Basham and Granville’s Elle Mortimer recently received All-Ohio honors from the Ohio High School Volleyball Coaches Association. Caudill, a senior, was named to the Division VII first team. top.title: Trusting Youth – It’s What Sunderland Does Best
top.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Sunderland player Jules Ahoka applauds the fans after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Chelsea FC at Stadium of Light on November 08, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jules Ahoka was handed his first Premier League appearance very early in the 1-0 win over Chelsea, being thrown into the mix with just minutes on the clock after Granit Xhaka went down injured. We’d seen a decent amount of him in other competitions, and few can argue that, either in Europe or the League Cup, he’d looked out of place despite barely playing any senior football before his move from Belgium in the summer. Ahoka came with a promising reputation, but there’s no doubting he was raw – and still is. However, the way he’s settled into the side is both a relief and exciting. There was a belief that he’d come in to be Xhaka’s understudy, and recent displays have left us feeling positive. If Ahoka is set to enjoy a breakthrough season in the Premier League, he’ll be another success story for Sunderland, proving it’s worth giving a youth player a first-team chance. Since Kyril Louis-Dreyfus took over, a recurring theme under the club’s head coaches has been trusting young players in the side. Some of these have been academy products, and although many have come and gone in the last few years, Chris Rigg is an example of a player who has been patient and earned his chance in the top flight and Europe. Timur Tutyerov, who joined the club as a teenager, has been trusted to lead the line on numerous occasions this season and has two goals to his name in six starts. It’s all about having faith in these players, and we’re seeing the rewards coming through with some top performances this season from the likes of Tutyerov and Ahoka. During the Championship promotion season, we were often told we didn’t have the experience to achieve anything and that our reliance on youth would be our downfall. This was followed by claims that we would struggle in the Premier League because we had too many young players without top-flight experience. As we reach the quarter-way mark of this third season of the RLB era, youth plays a key role in our team, whether that be through players we’ve signed from overseas or players produced and/or developed on Wearside. Ahoka is the talk of the town at the moment, and rightly so, but it’s probably not a bad idea to err on the side of caution and not get too carried away. However, he could end up playing a big role in the next few games if the injury that forced Xhaka off early against Chelsea is worse than anticipated. We’ve got a weekend off now, which I think is well timed – it’s always nice to go into an international break with a win under your belt. top.title: Australia captain Pat Cummins spotted in heated conversation with wife Becky in first public appearance since Khawaja’s Sandpaper claims
top.description: NEW DELHI: Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins has been spotted having what appeared to be a heated conversation with his wife, Becky, on a Sydney street. The incident marks his first public appearance since former Australian batter Usman Khawaja made fresh claims about the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as "Sandpaper-gate". According to footage published by The Australian on Wednesday, Cummins and Becky were seen having an animated discussion before heading inside a nearby property. Cummins, dressed casually in a T-shirt and shorts, appeared to remain relatively quiet during the exchange. The Australian captain is currently resting from the country's two white-ball series against England as he prepares for four upcoming Test matches against New Zealand. Fresh claims bring Sandpaper scandal back into focus The incident comes amid renewed controversy after Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian dressing room knew about the plan to tamper with the ball during the 2018 Test series in South Africa. Former opener David Warner, who was also involved in the scandal, has supported Khawaja's claims. In his autobiography Sabr, released on Tuesday, Khawaja shared his account of the events that resulted in Cricket Australia suspending Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. When asked about the possibility of Khawaja revealing details that differed from the findings of the official investigation, Cummins had earlier said: “It’s obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times,” Cummins said. “It was dealt with then, all I can say is as a group we’ve moved on. Very happy with the last eight or nine years, how we’ve been as a group and evolved. He didn’t go into too much detail . . . As always it was ‘no worries, you can tell your story, that’s fine’.” Khawaja refuses to reveal more details Khawaja has since cancelled his remaining media appearances for the book after facing tough questions on ABC's 7.30 program. During the interview, he was asked whether he was upset that the bowlers had not admitted knowing about the plan to rough up the ball using sandpaper. “I’ll say again, I’ve given my statement about what happened the game before,” Khawaja said. “I was very open and honest to what I saw and what conversations I had. Sometimes I’m very specific on things, and sometimes I’m a bit vague on things, and I do it on purpose because I’m trying to tell a story.” When questioned further about the bowlers' involvement, he refused to comment. “I’m just not going … I’m not going to entertain that,” Khawaja said. “I’m not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment.”

top.description: Alan Durban’s third – and, as it would turn out, final – season at Sunderland had picked up after a slow start that saw the club with just one win in the first six Division One games. A 1-0 victory over Bob Paisley’s Liverpool at Anfield in October, and a 2-1 win against Arsenal at Highbury, had certainly shown that the team was no pushover, and had higher aspirations than finishing just three points clear of the relegation zone, as they had done the previous campaign. After the trip to Highbury, Sunderland had faced a midweek Milk Cup trip to Norwich – a nil-nil scoreline drawing the ire of Canaries striker Mick Channon, who said: “We would never go away and play like they did. In fact, I’m glad we don’t play like that otherwise Mick Channon would have retired by now.” I’m glad I don’t refer to myself in the third person, Mick. That meant a Roker replay would soon follow – but in the meantime the lads were looking to build on the three points in North London with another three at home to Watford. It would be no small ask. Watford, under the headline-grabbing stewardship of Elton John, and the exceptionally promising managerial ability of Graham Taylor, had finished second in the First Division the season before. 1982/83 had been their first season ever in the top flight, with Taylor guiding them quickly up the leagues since taking over the Fourth Division club in 1977. For Sunderland, progress had been rather more sedate. While Durban – who’d taken over the permanent reins from Ken Knighton in the summer of 1981 – had been stifled by a lack of funds to really take the team forward at pace, he’d built a smart, young squad that, while capable of producing some excellent displays was also, predictable, a little inconsistent. Progress is rarely linear, yet the feeling was the team was heading steadily in the right direction. Watford’s achievements, however, showed that sometimes success could be achieved at a greater pace – albeit with a bit of spend. From taking over at Watford to achieving top flight promotion, Taylor had spent £1.38m – recouping around £500,000 in player sales. Sunderland, in the same timeframe, spent similarly. But, while Sunderland had spent serious money for the time on the likes of Claudio Marangoni and Ally McCoist, Watford’s investments in the likes of Gerry Armstrong, Wilf Rostron, Ross Jenkins and Pat Rice brought greater value for money. (Photo by Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images Dear Roker Report, I last wrote in over five years ago and thought long and hard about writing again after making a vow not to do so then. However, I was so disappointed and saddened last week to hear Martin proposing that Régis Le Bris should be sacked before the Chelsea game. Let me try to explain. My background I’m 82 years of age, having been an active supporter since 1955, and have experienced many ups and even more downs during that time. I come from a family of Sunderland fans. My grandfather was one of the 75,118 fans who attended the FA Cup match against Derby County on 8 March 1933. My father took a day off work to join me in 1973 when we beat our fiercest rivals, ”Dirty” Leeds United, against all the odds. Some of my best memories came after times when we were up against it, and four games stand out, with two against the team we beat on Sunday – Chelsea. 10 September 1955: The only time we’ve won after being 3-0 down, winning 4-3 against Chelsea, the reigning champions. Len Shackleton was the star that day. 18 May 1962: All we had to do was take a draw against Chelsea at home to win promotion. Chelsea’s manager, Tommy Docherty, got his team to cynically kick us off the park, and Tommy Harmer got a lucky deflection to give them a 1-0 win. We went on to win promotion the following year with ”Dirty” Leeds United. 16 December 1972: Along with a paltry crowd of 11,523, I watched us scrape a 0-0 draw against Preston North End. Five months later, we beat Leeds at Wembley with my heroes Monty, Watson, Hughes and Tueart. 25 May 1998: We lost at Wembley to Charlton Athletic, 4-4 and 7-6 on penalties. The next season, we won the Championship with a record points tally. The point of all this is to emphasise the importance of supporting our dear team, even during the darkest of days. We need perspective and objectivity from our Roker Report pundits, and not negativity, which gets you nowhere, Martin. Let’s, for a second, look at Régis’ record. From a previous position of 16th in the Championship, with the same players, he got us to the play-offs. MILWAUKEE — The Lakers used the third quarter to take control Wednesday night. By the end of it, Austin Reaves was out with a heel injury. Luka Dončić later followed him to the locker room. A 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks extended the Lakers’ winning streak to seven games, but the health of their starting backcourt became the more pressing concern as Los Angeles improved to 11-2. Dončić scored 32 points, and Sandro Mamukelashvili supplied 23 off the bench as the Lakers completed their third consecutive road victory. They outscored Milwaukee 33-23 in the third quarter to create separation, giving themselves room to withstand the late departures. Reaves finished with 18 points, five assists and three steals before leaving in the third quarter with a left heel injury. Coach JJ Redick said afterward that X-rays were negative, with additional imaging scheduled for Thursday. Reaves appeared to hurt his heel upon landing after a dunk attempt. He tried to play through it before heading to the locker room and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Dončić gave the Lakers another scare in the fourth quarter when he twisted his ankle on a made 3-pointer while being fouled by Kyle Kuzma. top.title: Student Loan: Parents, NANS offer tips on how to stop double dipping by beneficiaries

(Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart was ejected from the 115-108 win over the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday after attempting to punch Warriors center Charles Bassey. top.title: AWS distills its cloud into a local emulator that runs on your PC
top.description: AWS has released an emulator that kind-of-almost lets you use its cloud on a PC. As explained in the GitHub repository for the prosaically named “AWS Emulator,” the tool “is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint.” The emulator doesn’t replicate the whole AWS cloud, instead offering its APIs. “You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI),” the repo explains. Because those tests never touch the AWS cloud, the tool is free to use. AWS wrote the emulator in Rust, a choice that senior specialist solutions architect Daniel Abib wrote helps to ensure the tool “stays light on CPU and memory on a laptop.” The emulator tool doesn’t replicate the entire AWS cloud. Abib said it supports the APIs of AWS services that have an API model in the AWS API models repository on GitHub . The Register found over 1,300 items on that page. While the tool lets developers test APIs, it doesn’t replicate anywhere near all the features of the Amazonian cloud. “It doesn’t evaluate IAM [Identity and Access Management] policies the way AWS does, and each emulator acts as a single account, with no cross-account or cross-Region behavior,” Abib wrote, adding “How closely it matches AWS varies by service and feature.” AWS publishes “fidelity scores” that detail how closely the emulator works on different AWS services. Amazon tries to achieve full fidelity, so the emulator produces the same results as AWS for valid API calls, and the same errors for invalid ones. Coding agents can also drive the Emulator, an option The Register mentions because AWS advises the easiest way to check if a project will work with the tool is to use the aws-emulator skill for AI coding agents. “With the skill, your agent finds the AWS operations and resources that your project depends on. It checks them against the fidelity tests and fidelity scores for the emulator. It then tells you which parts of your project you can rely on the emulator for, and which ones might behave differently from AWS,” according to AWS documentation. AWS has made the emulator available as an RPM or Debian package. Mac and PC users will need to run Docker and an image of the Emulator. “You install the emulator, start it, and point your tools at the local endpoint,” Abib instructed. “When AWS Emulator starts, it generates its own credentials, a config file, and a certificate, and writes them to ~/.aws/emulator/9297/ . You set environment variables so the AWS SDK talks to your laptop instead of AWS, and your application code stays unchanged.” “From there, your existing tests, CLI scripts, and coding agents keep working the way they already do. A unit test that creates an Amazon DynamoDB table, writes an item, and reads it back is the same test, and it runs on your machine without a deployment.” The cloud colossus’s intent appears, as ever, to encourage more use of its cloud – in this case by satisfying developers their code will run w

top.title: Predators catch Ducks slipping, snap Anaheim streaks
top.description: Alexander Kerfoot #14 of the Nashville Predators defends the puck from Sam Colangelo #12 of the Anaheim Ducks during an NHL regular season game against the Anaheim Ducks on November 11, 2026 at Honda Center in Anaheim, California. ANAHEIM, Calif. – For so many recent nights, so much had gone the way of the Anaheim Ducks with eight straight games of five or more goals. However, on some nights, it just doesn’t bounce your way at all. Riding their own five-game winning streak, the Nashville Predators finished opportunities where the Ducks simply did not in the face of a stout goaltending performance from Justus Annunen in a 4-2 Nashville win on Wednesday at Honda Center. Anaheim (9-8-1, 19 points) snaps its five-game winning streak and its white hot offensive run, while Nashville pushed out to its sixth straight win. Cutter Gauthier continued his ludicrous goal-scoring streak, as the puck found him in the first period for his seventh straight game with a strike and his 14th goal in that span. Gauthier tied Corey Perry (2013-14) for the third-longest streak in team history. Teemu Selanne owns the two longest streaks at eight games (1998-99) and 11 games (1997-98). Mikael Granlund pulled the Ducks back within one late in the third period, 3-2, on a one-timer from Beckett Sennecke, who made up for his second missed breakaway with the feed. Jayden Struble evened it up for the Predators in the first period, as he pushed forward into open space where Travis Mitchell and Tristan Luneau jumped up into the play and couldn’t break it up. Nashville went ahead late in the second period, when Nils Höglander ripped off a highlight reel stunner, 2-1. Jackson LaCombe vacated the front of the net to make a play, but it went behind him to Höglander, who went between his legs and top shelf for the finish. It was a two-goal lead for Nashville midway through the third period, even if no one knew it immediately. Anaheim couldn’t clear the zone, and newly acquired Shane Wright found a rebound in the slot and shot it off the center post in the back of the net. The puck came out so quickly, no one immediately registered it as a goal, but on review, it was all the way in, 3-1. Nashville got insurance by getting past a pinching Drew Helleson, and Mavrik Borque fed Steven Stamkos around a sprawling Jackson LaCombe to reinstate the two-goal lead, 4-2. Laurent Brossoit stopped 18 of 22 shots in his fifth start in over a week with Anaheim. Lukáš Dostál was the back-up, and Ville Husso was a healthy scratch. Justus Annunen made 25 saves for the Predators with over 2.12 goals saved above expected on the night. Anaheim continues its four-game homestand with the first half of a back-to-back against the New York Islanders on Saturday. The Ducks will host Calgary on Sunday before hitting the road for a four-game trip.

As a fellow of Mujeres Por Africa and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, she sits at the intersection between biodiversity and cutting edge technology. With a PhD in herbal medicine, Odimegwu is a herbal medicine expert who got a grant from Gates Foundation to train African researchers on women’s health. According to her, women’s health has always been regulated because it’s complicated and what is complicating it is the hormones which can be up in the morning, down by afternoon. “It’s nature. It’s how we’re built, so it shouldn’t cause confusion. I didn’t know that other people were interested in the topic”, she told Vanguard. My area of research is biological patterns and I came across something very interesting. For many years they have been using broccoli to prevent certain gynecological cancers so as a researcher, I wanted to know what was in it. So, broccoli attacks inflammation and some people believe cancer is from inflammation”. Odimegwu wanted to be sure broccoli that is grown in Nigeria is the same as that broccoli. “My first degree was in Botany so I know about plants. I did some research. I got some in Jos, carried some down to Lagos and carried out the research to find out if broccoli’s Sulforaphane could modulate hormones in animals. The result I got was what I presented in Brazil. nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, also known as Anwar, a senior commander of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), alongside several of his fighters has brought major relief not only to the people of Ondo State but to the entire southern Nigeria. Ohida, who took over the coordination of ISWAP’s central and southern regional activities following the 2023 arrest of his superior, Abu Ikrimah (Abu Uwais) inside an Ondo forest, was killed during an intelligence-led operation deep inside the Owo Forest, Ondo State, early this month. nigeria.title: 4 dead, many hospitalised in Benue after consuming herbal mixture
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru Makurdi —No fewer than four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are battling for their lives in hospital after allegedly consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. It was gathered that the incident occurred after three men, identified as Magani, Mohamed and Kala, allegedly sold herbal preparations suspected to contain poisonous substances to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju township, last weekend. According to the eyewitness, “The development gained attention when some of those, who drank the mixture and their loved ones raised the alarm on November 2, 2026, after several residents, who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations started developing similar symptoms. “While the first victim reportedly died Tuesday morning, the second died in the early hours of Wednesday, and the third and fourth victims died later on November 4, 2026. “As we speak, over 14 other victims are currently battling for their lives, with many of them said to be in critical condition.” He disclosed that the three suspects allegedly involved in the sale of the herbal mixture were apprehended by the leadership of the Igede Youth Council, in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership, and subsequently handed over to the police in Oju. “We have been told that the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters has transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command, where the suspects are currently undergoing investigation,” he said. Speaking while handing over the suspects to the police, President of the Igede Youth Council, John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State government to ensure a thorough investigation of the incident and guarantee that justice was served. Ozzidi said the Igede youths had deliberately refrained from taking the law into their hands, resisting the temptation to subject the suspects to jungle justice. He explained that their decision to allow the law to take its course demonstrated their confidence in the state government to ensure justice is done in the matter. The youth leader also urged political officeholders from the area to follow up on the case to ensure that the deceased victims got justice and that the circumstances surrounding the suspected poisoning were fully established. Contacted, the Chairman of Oju council, Mr. Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he was yet to obtain the exact number of fatalities. nigeria.title: The US built world’s greatest card system
nigeria.description: By YVONNE-FAITH ELAIGWU The history of payments is, in many ways, the history of making value easier to move. We started at barter and are now at electronic transfers, with stablecoins suggesting that the next evolution is here. New payment methods rarely make their predecessors useless. Cash did not immediately eliminate barter. Cards did not eliminate cheques. Account-to-account payments will not eliminate cards. But payments evolve. And one of the most interesting examples of that evolution can be found in an unlikely comparison: Nigeria and the United States. The United States built perhaps the world’s greatest card ecosystem. Nigeria just seems to have built past it. The American card system is extraordinary. Over decades, the U.S. built an ecosystem connecting consumers, merchants, issuing banks, acquiring banks, and card networks. Around it grew credit bureaus, credit scores, revolving credit, chargebacks, fraud protection, loyalty points, airline miles, and billions of dollars of rewards. Consequently, Americans have a compelling reason to use cards. And use them, they do. Data from the Federal Reserve show that credit-card payments reached 67.1 billion transactions in 2024, while ACH processed an enormous $104.06 trillion in 2024. America, therefore, doesn’t lack account-to-account infrastructure. The difference is where A2A sits in everyday consumer behaviour. Walk into an American store, and the natural question is still: Which card am I using? In Nigeria, increasingly, a different question is asked: “What is your account number?” That difference is more significant than it appears. Nigeria took another road. Nigeria never developed America’s deep credit-card culture. Debit cards became widespread, but cards did not become as deeply embedded in the country’s economic architecture as they did in America. Instead, Nigeria increasingly solved digital payments at the bank-account level. At the centre of this transformation is the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System and its NIBSS Instant Payment platform, built to operate 24/7 with most transactions settling in under one second. This infrastructure changed behaviour. Any individual or company can pay another individual or merchant, and the transaction can be executed on a Friday evening or a Sunday morning. The expectation is still remarkably simple: the money should arrive now. That expectation is one of Nigeria’s greatest payment achievements. America’s success may be part of its problem. This is where the comparison becomes fascinating. America isn’t stuck on cards because it cannot build something better. It may be stuck on cards partly because cards work so well. The merchant already has the terminal. The consumer already has the card. The bank earns card revenue. Visa and Mastercard provide enormous networks. The CJN also used the occasion to launch the second edition of the Judicial Electoral Manual (JEM), which she said will help judicial officers locate relevant authorities, appreciate the development of the law and approach recurring issues with greater clarity. According to the CJN, by bringing together the relevant constitutional provisions, the Electoral Act 2026, applicable practice directions and judicial decisions, the Manual provides a useful resource for judicial officers and other stakeholders in the electoral adjudicatory process. She was quick to warn, however, that it should serve only as a guide and a reference tool. nigeria.description: The United Nations General Assembly has, for the first time, formally endorsed a global shift away from the centuries-old Mercator map in favour of projections that show Africa—and other equatorial regions—in their true relative size. This “Correct the Map” resolution, spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group and backed by the African Union, passed by 164 votes to one, with six abstentions. While non-binding, it marks a watershed moment in how the world visually represents the continent—and, by extension, how it perceives Africa’s weight in global affairs. The root of the misrepresentation lies in the Mercator projection, devised in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator for maritime navigation. To keep compass bearings straight, Mercator preserved angles and shapes—but at the cost of area. The result: landmasses near the poles, such as Europe, North America and Greenland, are visually enlarged, while those near the equator, including Africa, Latin America and South Asia, are shrunk. On typical Mercator wall maps, Greenland appears roughly the same size as Africa. In reality, Africa covers about 30.3 million square kilometres, making it around 14 times larger than Greenland’s 2.1 million square kilometres. This is not a minor quirk; it is a systematic visual bias baked into the most widely used world map for nearly five centuries. The resolution encourages governments, schools, international organisations, media houses and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections, especially the Equal Earth projection, whenever comparative continental size matters. It frames map distortion as more than a technical issue—calling it a cognitive, educational, cultural and geopolitical problem that has contributed to the symbolic minimisation of Africa in the global imagination. While symbolic correction matters, Africa’s greatest vulnerabilities lie in structural exploitation and escalating insecurity, notably from Islamist insurgencies across the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and parts of the Horn. Map reform must be paired with hard-edged action on multiple fronts. First, curb external exploitation and illicit financial flows by tightening transparency on extractives, choking illicit financial flows through cross-border tax cooperation, and rebalancing investment terms to prioritise local content and value addition. nigeria.title: Beyond The Sole: How Nigerian Artist Eugene Is Turning Waste Into Beauty For A Better World
nigeria.description: An art project that started as a final-year assessment at Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State, Nigeria, has turned into a full-time career for Konboye Eugene. In his studio in Kuto, Abeokuta, Ogun State, the Nigerian artist is giving discarded footwear a new lease of life, transforming them into colourful portraits. “I’ve been a full-time studio practitioner for about seven years now. I started when I was in my final year at Auchi Polytechnic, where I studied painting,” Eugene said. “It started as an assignment for me when I was in school. But over the course of my practice, I have become a bit more environmentally aware.” ﻿ Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Materials ‘Everywhere, Anywhere’ Eugene’s craft draws attention to the environmental impact of discarded footwear and the need for better ways to manage waste. “I source my material through landfills, the streets, literally everywhere, anywhere,” he added. This image shows Eugene assessing discarded footwear he used for his artwork. (Photo: ChannelsTV/Kenny Akinwunmi) The artist shares the detailed process of how he brings each work of art to life. “My process entails getting the materials first, after which we wash them. After we wash them, we have to select and separate them according to their colours, tones, and values.” “I work in two different ways. There’s the assemblage part, where I assemble the footwear. And there’s also the tapestry, where I have to break them into tiny circles and fix them together using copper and aluminium wire,” Eugene explained. Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Creating each piece of artwork comes with its challenges, as Eugene says the process can take between two and six months, depending on its size and complexity. “There are a whole lot of challenges that come with the work. There are times when we’re working and have creative blockages. And also, because we work with sharp objects like knives, needles, and all that, there’s also the hazard that comes with it. “I think we work between two to six months, depending on the size and complexity of what we’re working on in the studio,” he said. For Eugene, the message goes beyond the finished artwork, as he hopes his work will change how people perceive and handle discarded materials. “These are materials that are known to be non-biodegradable, meaning all the footwear that I’ve used over the course of the years, they’re all out there. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30 MSCI will remove Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, from the MSCI USA Index as of the close of Nov. 30, the index provider said Wednesday, after a new screen classified the company as a non-operating issuer. The decision is part of MSCI’s November 2026 Index Review , posted shortly after 5 p.m. ET. Official additions and deletions lists show Strategy (MSTR) out of its USA Index, which also takes it out of the broader MSCI World and ACWI indexes. The same review deletes Japan’s Metaplanet from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index and uranium holder Yellow Cake from the MSCI United Kingdom Small Cap Index, and it removes Iceland’s Skel Fjárfestingafélag from the MSCI Iceland Frontier Markets Small Cap Index and micro-cap Upexi from the USA Micro Cap Index. All five had already been marked Deleted on MSCI’s potential-impact list , built on Sept. 30 financial data and Oct. 9 market values. Strategy is the only large-cap name in the group and, on that October list, accounted for more than 90% of the five companies’ combined float-adjusted market value. The company held 850,364 bitcoin as of Nov. 8, acquired at an average price of $75,456 a coin, or $64.16 billion in aggregate. Strategy shares closed at $122.35, up 1.06%, then slipped 1.51% to $120.50 in after-hours trading as of 5:34 p.m. ET. How the MSCI screen works The rule does not mention bitcoin. The index first checks whether a company’s operating assets equal at least 50% of total assets. Issuers that fail that core screen face five financial ratios, and a company flagged on four or more of them is ineligible for the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes. Buffers limit turnover. A company outside the indexes cannot be added if it fails the ineligibility screen in either of its two most recent annual filing periods, but a current constituent is removed only if it fails in each of them. The index said it may also use the most recent interim filing. MSCI also said Wednesday that the same non-operating treatment will apply to the MSCI US Index Series. The screen replaces an approach aimed squarely at crypto. The index first proposed in late 2025 to exclude companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of total assets, then dropped that plan in January and opened a broader consultation in August. It adopted the new methodology on Oct. 15, with minor modifications, and said it would end the interim measures it had placed on those companies in October 2025, including a freeze on share-count increases and a deferral of additions. entertainment.title: Olumide Oworu Declares House of Representatives Bid for Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027
entertainment.description: Olumide Oworu has declared his candidacy for the Federal House of Representatives to represent Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Actor and media personality Olumide Oworu has declared his intention to contest for the Federal House of Representatives seat for Surulere Constituency 1 in the 2027 general elections. He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. However, administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot. Olumide Oworu’s official campaign poster for the House of Representatives seat representing Surulere Constituency 1 under the Allied Peoples Movement. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Reflecting on that experience in his candidacy announcement on Instagram, Olumide said the support he received from young people in Surulere had strengthened his belief in their readiness for more active participation in governance. “Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. Announcing his candidacy, he said he looked forward to continued support as he and his supporters worked towards what he described as a mission to “Reset Nigeria”. Olumide Oworu is contesting for a legislative seat in Surulere Constituency 1 under the APM platform. entertainment.description: Awar Odhiang featured in Vogue wearing a floral printed dress and sculpted oversized rose headpiece. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Remember the model who turned the finale of Matthieu Blazy ‘s first Chanel show into one of the most talked-about runway moments of 2025? That was Awar Odhiang, and she has another major reason to celebrate. The South Sudanese-Canadian model has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026. The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. She is now represented by major modelling agencies across London, Milan, Paris and New York. Awar Odhiang walking the red carpet at the 2026 Met Gala in New York City. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her runway résumé includes shows for Prada, Versace, Miu Miu, Saint Laurent and Jacquemus, but it was her appearance at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2026 show in October 2025 that introduced her to an even wider audience. Closing Matthieu Blazy’s first collection for the fashion house, Awar wore the show’s bridal look, featuring an oversized white shirt and a voluminous, colourful feathered skirt. But it was what happened at the finale that captured everyone’s attention. As the models gathered for their final walk, Awar broke formation, smiling, clapping and twirling in her skirt. When Blazy appeared, she ran towards him and embraced him. The spontaneous moment quickly went viral, with fashion fans celebrating the joy she brought to the runway. It was also a historic appearance: Awar became only the third Black woman to close a Chanel show in the house’s 115-year history, after Alek Wek and Adut Akech. Model of the Year 2026 winner Awar Odhiang backstage at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Since then, her career has continued to gather pace. Awar Odhiang in Daniel Roseberry’s Schiaparelli Spring 2026 Haute Couture collection in Paris. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her Model of the Year recognition celebrates a remarkable year of runway, editorial and campaign work, as well as the influence she continues to have beyond the catwalk. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. sports.title: Houston Rockets beat Golden State Warriors in wild one that included Marcus Smart throwing a punch
sports.description: Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) shot in the first half of game action at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Even with Stephen Curry playing just six minutes before leaving with an injury, the Houston Rockets and Golden State Warriors played their usual chaotic battle. The Rockets survived against the short-handed Warriors with a 115-108 victory Wednesday at Toyota Center, but not before they lost Marcus Smart for throwing a punch at Charles Bassey. When the dust settled the Rockets (9-3) dealt the Warriors (8-4), who were on an eight-game winning streak, their first loss since Oct. 24. Amen Thompson had a huge third quarter for the Rockets, scoring 15 of his 19 points in the third. Kevin Durant led Houston with 20 points. Alperen Şengün finished an assist shy of a triple-double with 19 points, 13 rebounds and 9 assists. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg finished with 25 points and 10 rebounds. Things got tense late in the third quarter, when Smart went face-to-face with the Warriors' big man during a dead ball. After the two exchanged words, Smart unleashed a right hand that appeared to graze Bassey's cheek. Smart was ejected, but already had walked off the court and into the tunnel, knowing his fate. Bassey made one of two free throws after the fracas to cut the Rockets' lead to 85-77. The Warriors showed further life early in the fourth quarter with Georges Niang and De'Anthony Melton hitting back-to-back 3-pointers to get within three points with nine minutes remaining. However, the Rockets scored eight straight, including two 3s by Reed Sheppard to stretch the lead back to double digits. When Curry, who entered the night averaging 30.6 points per game, went out with abdominal soreness just six minutes into the game, it looked like it might be a stress-free night for the Rockets. Curry went to the locker room midway through the first quarter with the Warriors trailing 19-10. With no Curry to chase all over the court, Houston stretched that lead to 35-20 by the end of the first quarter. However, Curry being out seemed to unlock Lendeborg, the early front-runner for Rookie of the Year. The 11th pick in the draft out of Michigan scored 18 points in the first half, all coming after Curry's injury. He scored in a variety of ways, knocking down a couple 3-pointers, while also working the boards and getting out on the break. Lendeborg keyed a 9-2 run late in the first half that tied the game, hitting a 26-footer and a midrange jumper during the run that knotted things at 49. The Rockets closed the half with a 7-2 run of their own to enter halftime with a 56-51 edge. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. sports.title: Houston Astros' Yordan Alvarez wins AL's Hank Aaron Award among accolades at MLB Awards
sports.description: Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez, pictured with MLB Network's Siera Santos at Wednesday's awards show, took home the prestigious Hank Aaron Award as well as three other accolades on the eve of the MVP announcement. (Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) LAS VEGAS - Yordan Alvarez was named the American League recipient of this year's Hank Aaron Award on Wednesday night in another nod to the Houston Astros slugger's prolific season. The Hank Aaron Award recognizes the top offensive performer in each league. Alvarez joins Jose Altuve as Astros players to win the award, which was introduced in 1999 to mark the 25th anniversary of Aaron breaking Babe Ruth's career home-run record. Altuve won the award in 2017 , the same year he was named the American League Most Valuable Player. Alvarez will learn Thursday whether he joins Altuve and Jeff Bagwell as Astros players to win a league MVP award. Alvarez garnered multiple honors at the MLB Awards show, which was held Wednesday night in Las Vegas with the slugger attending in person. Alvarez was also named AL Comeback Player of the Year, the Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter and the All-MLB First Team designated hitter. Winners of the Hank Aaron Award were announced with Billye Aaron - the widow of Hank Aaron, who died in 2021 - among those on stage. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs was voted the National League winner. Alvarez delivered a brief comment on stage after he was named the AL winner. "It means a lot for me, especially because I wear the number 44," Alvarez said, referencing the number also worn by Aaron, at the awards event streamed by MLB.com. "I've been working really hard for this moment and it's really special for me to be part of and see my name on this trophy." To determine the Hank Aaron Award winners, a panel of 10 former winners and Hall of Famers vote on the list of 10 finalists from each league. Astros Hall of Famer Craig Biggio was part of this year's panel. Fans were allowed to vote from the list of finalists, as well. After playing in just 48 games in 2025 due to hand and ankle injuries, Alvarez this season led the majors in batting average (.316), on-base percentage (.432) and slugging percentage (.601), becoming the third Astros player to win a league batting title. Alvarez tied for second in the AL in home runs (42) and ranked second in runs batted in (106), recording career-high marks in both. sports.title: Trusting Youth – It’s What Sunderland Does Best
sports.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Sunderland player Jules Ahoka applauds the fans after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Chelsea FC at Stadium of Light on November 08, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jules Ahoka was handed his first Premier League appearance very early in the 1-0 win over Chelsea, being thrown into the mix with just minutes on the clock after Granit Xhaka went down injured. We’d seen a decent amount of him in other competitions, and few can argue that, either in Europe or the League Cup, he’d looked out of place despite barely playing any senior football before his move from Belgium in the summer. Ahoka came with a promising reputation, but there’s no doubting he was raw – and still is. However, the way he’s settled into the side is both a relief and exciting. There was a belief that he’d come in to be Xhaka’s understudy, and recent displays have left us feeling positive. If Ahoka is set to enjoy a breakthrough season in the Premier League, he’ll be another success story for Sunderland, proving it’s worth giving a youth player a first-team chance. Since Kyril Louis-Dreyfus took over, a recurring theme under the club’s head coaches has been trusting young players in the side. Some of these have been academy products, and although many have come and gone in the last few years, Chris Rigg is an example of a player who has been patient and earned his chance in the top flight and Europe. Timur Tutyerov, who joined the club as a teenager, has been trusted to lead the line on numerous occasions this season and has two goals to his name in six starts. It’s all about having faith in these players, and we’re seeing the rewards coming through with some top performances this season from the likes of Tutyerov and Ahoka. During the Championship promotion season, we were often told we didn’t have the experience to achieve anything and that our reliance on youth would be our downfall. This was followed by claims that we would struggle in the Premier League because we had too many young players without top-flight experience. As we reach the quarter-way mark of this third season of the RLB era, youth plays a key role in our team, whether that be through players we’ve signed from overseas or players produced and/or developed on Wearside. Ahoka is the talk of the town at the moment, and rightly so, but it’s probably not a bad idea to err on the side of caution and not get too carried away. sports.title: Australia captain Pat Cummins spotted in heated conversation with wife Becky in first public appearance since Khawaja’s Sandpaper claims
sports.description: NEW DELHI: Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins has been spotted having what appeared to be a heated conversation with his wife, Becky, on a Sydney street. The incident marks his first public appearance since former Australian batter Usman Khawaja made fresh claims about the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as "Sandpaper-gate". According to footage published by The Australian on Wednesday, Cummins and Becky were seen having an animated discussion before heading inside a nearby property. Cummins, dressed casually in a T-shirt and shorts, appeared to remain relatively quiet during the exchange. The Australian captain is currently resting from the country's two white-ball series against England as he prepares for four upcoming Test matches against New Zealand. Fresh claims bring Sandpaper scandal back into focus The incident comes amid renewed controversy after Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian dressing room knew about the plan to tamper with the ball during the 2018 Test series in South Africa. Former opener David Warner, who was also involved in the scandal, has supported Khawaja's claims. In his autobiography Sabr, released on Tuesday, Khawaja shared his account of the events that resulted in Cricket Australia suspending Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. When asked about the possibility of Khawaja revealing details that differed from the findings of the official investigation, Cummins had earlier said: “It’s obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times,” Cummins said. “It was dealt with then, all I can say is as a group we’ve moved on. Very happy with the last eight or nine years, how we’ve been as a group and evolved. He didn’t go into too much detail . . . As always it was ‘no worries, you can tell your story, that’s fine’.” Khawaja refuses to reveal more details Khawaja has since cancelled his remaining media appearances for the book after facing tough questions on ABC's 7.30 program. During the interview, he was asked whether he was upset that the bowlers had not admitted knowing about the plan to rough up the ball using sandpaper. “I’ll say again, I’ve given my statement about what happened the game before,” Khawaja said. “I was very open and honest to what I saw and what conversations I had. Sometimes I’m very specific on things, and sometimes I’m a bit vague on things, and I do it on purpose because I’m trying to tell a story.” When questioned further about the bowlers' involvement, he refused to comment. “I’m just not going … I’m not going to entertain that,” Khawaja said. “I’m not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment.”

sports.title: Predators catch Ducks slipping, snap Anaheim streaks
sports.description: Alexander Kerfoot #14 of the Nashville Predators defends the puck from Sam Colangelo #12 of the Anaheim Ducks during an NHL regular season game against the Anaheim Ducks on November 11, 2026 at Honda Center in Anaheim, California. ANAHEIM, Calif. – For so many recent nights, so much had gone the way of the Anaheim Ducks with eight straight games of five or more goals. However, on some nights, it just doesn’t bounce your way at all. Riding their own five-game winning streak, the Nashville Predators finished opportunities where the Ducks simply did not in the face of a stout goaltending performance from Justus Annunen in a 4-2 Nashville win on Wednesday at Honda Center. Anaheim (9-8-1, 19 points) snaps its five-game winning streak and its white hot offensive run, while Nashville pushed out to its sixth straight win. Cutter Gauthier continued his ludicrous goal-scoring streak, as the puck found him in the first period for his seventh straight game with a strike and his 14th goal in that span. Gauthier tied Corey Perry (2013-14) for the third-longest streak in team history. Teemu Selanne owns the two longest streaks at eight games (1998-99) and 11 games (1997-98). Mikael Granlund pulled the Ducks back within one late in the third period, 3-2, on a one-timer from Beckett Sennecke, who made up for his second missed breakaway with the feed. Jayden Struble evened it up for the Predators in the first period, as he pushed forward into open space where Travis Mitchell and Tristan Luneau jumped up into the play and couldn’t break it up. Nashville went ahead late in the second period, when Nils Höglander ripped off a highlight reel stunner, 2-1. Jackson LaCombe vacated the front of the net to make a play, but it went behind him to Höglander, who went between his legs and top shelf for the finish. It was a two-goal lead for Nashville midway through the third period, even if no one knew it immediately. Anaheim couldn’t clear the zone, and newly acquired Shane Wright found a rebound in the slot and shot it off the center post in the back of the net. The puck came out so quickly, no one immediately registered it as a goal, but on review, it was all the way in, 3-1. Nashville got insurance by getting past a pinching Drew Helleson, and Mavrik Borque fed Steven Stamkos around a sprawling Jackson LaCombe to reinstate the two-goal lead, 4-2. Laurent Brossoit stopped 18 of 22 shots in his fifth start in over a week with Anaheim. Lukáš Dostál was the back-up, and Ville Husso was a healthy scratch. Justus Annunen made 25 saves for the Predators with over 2.12 goals saved above expected on the night. Anaheim continues its four-game homestand with the first half of a back-to-back against the New York Islanders on Saturday. The Ducks will host Calgary on Sunday before hitting the road for a four-game trip.

sports.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 24: Matvei Michkov #39 of the Philadelphia Flyers warms up before a game against the Anaheim Ducks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 24, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty There has been all sorts of speculation about the Montreal Canadiens being the top destination for Tampa Bay Lightning forward Nikita Kucherov. However, there are various issues that won’t necessarily make Montreal the best destination for the 33-year-old forward. So, it might actually be a good idea for the Canadiens to forget about Kucherov and pivot their attention to another Russian forward, Matvei Michkov. Michkov has gotten a barrage of attention over the last 24 hours following Kevin Weekes’ report that he had requested a trade out of Philadelphia. And while the Flyers have vowed, like the Lightning, that they’re not trading Michkov, the chatter isn’t going away. **Breaking News** 🚨 📰 From multiple league sources, with the Flyers unimpressive start and internal turmoil, Michkov would likely want a new start elsewhere. He's in the last year of his contract & is a prime trade candidate moving forward. #HockeyX pic.twitter.com/4mYzKiN42G — Kevin Weekes (@KevinWeekes) November 10, 2026 And when looking at the practicality of the matter, the Habs may be better off passing on the uber-expensive Kucherov, and focus on the much younger, much more affordable Michkov. The biggest issue, of course, will be the asking price on the 21-year-old. The Flyers won’t let him go for peanuts, but landing Michkov won’t likely cost Montreal Michael Hage or Alexander Zharovsky . What it would cost the Canadiens is a center. And they may not necessarily have one that the Philly would like. But then again, there may be a willingness to make something happen, especially if the Flyers figure to lose Michkov. Matvei Michkov would fit what the Canadiens need Start with the Ivan Demidov connection, because it makes for a compelling argument. Michkov and Demidov are fellow countrymen who have gotten to know each other. They often speak to the point where Michkov was among the first to reach out to Demidov to congratulate him on his first NHL game. Also, they play similar positions, even if they approach the game differently. That’s a good thing. Michkov also shoots left and can play either wing, while Demidov plays the right side. That’s why slotting them together on one line isn’t hard to picture. Then there’s the age. Michkov is 21, which fits the mold of the young players the Canadiens are building around. technology.title: AWS distills its cloud into a local emulator that runs on your PC
technology.description: AWS has released an emulator that kind-of-almost lets you use its cloud on a PC. As explained in the GitHub repository for the prosaically named “AWS Emulator,” the tool “is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint.” The emulator doesn’t replicate the whole AWS cloud, instead offering its APIs. “You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI),” the repo explains. Because those tests never touch the AWS cloud, the tool is free to use. AWS wrote the emulator in Rust, a choice that senior specialist solutions architect Daniel Abib wrote helps to ensure the tool “stays light on CPU and memory on a laptop.” The emulator tool doesn’t replicate the entire AWS cloud. Abib said it supports the APIs of AWS services that have an API model in the AWS API models repository on GitHub . The Register found over 1,300 items on that page. While the tool lets developers test APIs, it doesn’t replicate anywhere near all the features of the Amazonian cloud. “It doesn’t evaluate IAM [Identity and Access Management] policies the way AWS does, and each emulator acts as a single account, with no cross-account or cross-Region behavior,” Abib wrote, adding “How closely it matches AWS varies by service and feature.” AWS publishes “fidelity scores” that detail how closely the emulator works on different AWS services. Amazon tries to achieve full fidelity, so the emulator produces the same results as AWS for valid API calls, and the same errors for invalid ones. Coding agents can also drive the Emulator, an option The Register mentions because AWS advises the easiest way to check if a project will work with the tool is to use the aws-emulator skill for AI coding agents. “With the skill, your agent finds the AWS operations and resources that your project depends on. It checks them against the fidelity tests and fidelity scores for the emulator. It then tells you which parts of your project you can rely on the emulator for, and which ones might behave differently from AWS,” according to AWS documentation. AWS has made the emulator available as an RPM or Debian package. Mac and PC users will need to run Docker and an image of the Emulator. “You install the emulator, start it, and point your tools at the local endpoint,” Abib instructed. “When AWS Emulator starts, it generates its own credentials, a config file, and a certificate, and writes them to ~/.aws/emulator/9297/ . You set environment variables so the AWS SDK talks to your laptop instead of AWS, and your application code stays unchanged.” “From there, your existing tests, CLI scripts, and coding agents keep working the way they already do. A unit test that creates an Amazon DynamoDB table, writes an item, and reads it back is the same test, and it runs on your machine without a deployment.” The cloud colossus’s intent appears, as ever, to encourage more use of its cloud – in this case by satisfying developers their code will run w

technology.title: Disgraced former CA eMudhra blames buggy script for hopelessly weak certificates
technology.description: Former certification authority eMudhra has claimed a buggy Python script is the main reason it issued laughably insecure digital certificates. The company posted its account of the matter on Bugzilla where a user with the handle “Naveen Kumar ML” wrote “During a single key‑generation ceremony on 30 April 2025, sixteen subordinate (issuing) CA key pairs in eMudhra’s ‘B’ and ‘C’ series were generated correctly on a hardware security module and then processed through an approved wrap/unwrap round‑trip using a custom python key‑handling script.” eMudhra aimed to create eight ECDSA P-384 private keys which should have been 48 bytes long. But the script contained what Kumar described as “a bug/defect in the import code [which] resulted in a read‑back from the unwrapped object that truncated the private value, so the certified public keys correspond to private scalars below the expected range and are recoverable from public information.” The truncation is the key problem here, because it appears that eMudhra ignored 47 of the 48 bytes, producing its infamously insecure single-byte keys such as the number four. Whatever the nature of the bug, Kumar asserts it was “a custom script run only on an isolated ceremony host and was not a function of the emCA software.” eMudhra needed that script because “global supply chain constraints” meant it couldn’t acquire the hardware security modules (HSMs), devices that generate and store cryptographic keys, that it wanted to use when creating a set of certificates for use in the USA. It therefore used HSMs made by a company called Utimaco to generate keys and planned to transfer the keys it produced to a different set of HSMs from a company called Crypto4A. Kumar explained that eMudhra decided on that move, which is unusual, because changes to policy about provenance of certificates meant it had to generate new certs by the end of May. The plan went sour when the company didn’t notice the errors in its script and didn’t test the keys it created. The rest is history: a Mozilla team member noticed that the company’s keys were woefully weak and pointed out that attackers could therefore issue fraudulent certificates that allowed them to impersonate servers, observe traffic, or even modify data in transit. Browser-makers quickly tweaked their software so it would not recognize certs from eMudhra. The Indian business then quit the SSL/TLS certification business, which it said was never a major source of revenue but had suddenly become a severe source of embarrassment. Kumar’s new post lists three steps eMudhra will take to wind up its certification business, one of which will see the company “Put in place improvements motivated by findings of [an] independent review to strengthen our general PKI operations.” Sounds like a plan. ®

technology.title: Russian cloud Yandex says drone attacks on its datacenters caused data loss
technology.description: Russian cloud operator Yandex has admitted to data loss after a drone attack on one of its datacenters. The attack, which Ukrainian press said was ordered by Kyiv, happened in early October and caused a fire and subsequent outage at Yandex’s ru-central1-b availability zone. Subsequent strikes targeted more Yandex datacenters and disrupted more of the company’s cloud and payment services. On Tuesday, Yandex posted an update on its recovery efforts, which it spun as something of a triumph because it restored over 97 percent of customer data. Of course that also means the company lost 2.84 percent of customer data, which it blamed on “critical hardware damage and a lack of backups on the platform.” It’s unclear if Yandex’s use of the phrase “on the platform” indicates it doesn’t keep backups of its own cloud, if whatever resilience techniques it employs don’t create multiple copies of customer data, or if clients didn’t protect their data. Whatever happened, Yandex has decided to enable backups by default for all VMs customers create in its cloud. That decision will mean customers will consume and pay for more Yandex resources, unless they opt out of the automated backups. Given that drones damaged three Yandex locations, and the war with Ukraine continues, users have good reasons to consider alternatives to its services. Indeed, Yandex’s announcement of its recovery efforts links to a page extolling the virtues of a hybrid cloud when devising data protection strategies. That page also mentions Yandex’s own Stackland product, which brings its stack on-prem, as an example of a hybrid approach. On Wednesday the company also launched a new availability zone named ru-central1-f. Yandex didn’t say where it’s located, other than to say it’s in “a new location.” Interestingly, Yandex has imposed quotas that limit the amount of resources users can access in the new availability zone and says it can’t yet handle traffic to private endpoints at the new facility. Many nations have imposed sanctions that restrict sales of technology products to Russia. It’s therefore unsurprising that Yandex might struggle to provision enough infrastructure to allow untrammeled access to a new availability zone. ®

technology.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
technology.description: Datacenter power consumption in the US is growing roughly ten times faster than grid capacity, meaning facilities may soon need to find a large chunk of their own electricity from other sources. Surging demand for AI infrastructure is driving a wave of new server farms across America, but it is exposing long-term underinvestment in the grid networks required to deliver power where it's needed. Insurance broker Howden calculates that datacenters would need to source up to 58 percent of their power off the grid by 2030 just to keep their share of grid capacity from growing. Gartner warned in June that the energy consumed by AI datacenters is on track to grow 26 percent this year, and grid supply may be unable to keep pace with demand by the end of this decade. Howden's analysis of data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and S&P Global found that since the year 2000, power being fed to data campuses has risen 19 percent a year on average, while the electricity grid expanded capacity by just 2 percent per annum over the same period. Datacenters' share of US grid capacity was circa five percent in 2025, up from 0.1 percent in 2000 – a 50-fold increase. Management consultancy Bain & Company issued a report two years ago warning that energy companies must switch gear and invest in building out grid capacity faster , as energy draw by server farms is expected to more than double by 2030. This doesn't mean that datacenters are in danger of eating all of America's electricity, at least not in the immediate future. The graph makes it appear that the two lines are about to cross, but the chart uses different scales: 1,400 gigawatts on the left axis for grid capacity, versus just 80 on the right for datacenters. Keeping datacenters at five percent of grid capacity requires 110 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity by 2030, Howden estimates – an expansion it considers unlikely. Instead, it expects a combination of greater reliance on the grid, slower development at power-constrained sites, and alternative supplies. For the largest, most power-constrained projects, Howden warns that grid delays of two to six years could mean $800 million to $2.4 billion in forgone revenue. "Power availability is becoming one of the defining challenges of the datacenter boom," says Howden head of Natural Resources Stuart Adam. "As demand for AI infrastructure accelerates, developers are increasingly looking beyond traditional grid connections to secure the electricity they need." Howden's business is insurance, and so Adam also notes that on-site generation introduces new operational and financial exposures, as operators take greater responsibility for their power infrastructure. ®

science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such flight for the company in a six-day span. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m. EST (8:36 p.m. local California time; 0136 GMT on Nov. 12), kicking off a mission called USSF-627. Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov. 6, a Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission skyward from the site, which lies on California's gorgeous but often foggy central coast. A Falcon 9 first stage rests on a SpaceX drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-627 mission on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) We don't know much about USSF-627 or USSF-432; both are classified. Some experts have speculated , however, that each mission launched a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military branch track potential targets around the world. SpaceX didn't reveal details about either USSF-627 or USSF-432, and the company ended the webcast of both launches shortly after the first stages of their Falcon 9 rockets came back to Earth . In both cases, that touchdown occurred about 8.5 minutes after liftoff on the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange of Vandenberg in the Pacific Ocean. It was the seventh mission for USSF-627's Falcon 9 booster, which carries the designation 1103. Previous Booster 1103 missions NROL-179 | SDA-T1TL-E | SDA-T1TL-A | 3 Starlink missions USSF-627 was the 120th Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the rocket's 15th national-security flight of the year to date. Eighty-five of the 120 flights have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink broadband constellation in low Earth orbit , which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 is not on a record-breaking cadence this year. In 2025, the rocket flew a whopping 165 missions , and 122 of them were Starlink flights.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Moon, Venus and Spica Meet Explanation: Not all those who wander are lost. A night sky example is that planets wander, and in fact the very word “planet” comes from “wandering star” in Greek. As planets shift relative to fixed stars , they may appear from our perspective to get closer to other astronomical objects. Such meetings are called conjunctions . They don’t happen by chance, but follow the precise laws of celestial mechanics . This peaceful image , captured in Poland , shows the crescent Moon above the Tatra Mountains , and bright Venus close by, a little lower in the horizon. The bright star to the left of Venus is Spica in the constellation of Virgo , the Maiden. Spica is one of the brightest stars in the sky, only about 250 light-years away. It was found in 1890 that Spica is a binary star: two massive blue stars orbiting each other every 4 days. But earlier this year it was reported that Spica, the current companion of wandering Venus, is actually a triple system . Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next?
